title: Meeting Rooms II
description: Minimum rooms = max simultaneous meetings. Sort starts and ends separately, then sweep with two pointers — a meeting reuses a room iff its start is at or after the next ending. O(n log n).

notes: The starts/ends arrays are decoupled — pairing is irrelevant; only the timeline of events matters.
Strict `<`: a meeting starting exactly when another ends can reuse the room.
Equivalent min-heap solution: push end times, pop when the next start is ≥ heap top — same O(n log n).

questions.q: Why can starts and ends be sorted independently?
options: We only need the timeline of events, not which start pairs with which end
A meeting ends and frees a room
A new meeting begins before any current one ends — we need an additional room

questions.q: Why is the comparison `<` and not `<=`?
options: If a meeting starts exactly when one ends, the room can be reused — no new room needed

questions.explain: Sorting dominates; the sweep is linear.

exercises.prompt: Fill in two-pointer min meeting rooms.

blanks.hint: advance the ends pointer to free a room

L3.prompt: Implement `minMeetingRooms(intervals)` returning the minimum number of rooms. Log it for `[[0,30],[5,10],[15,20]]` then `[[7,10],[2,4]]`.
hints: Decouple starts and ends, sort both ascending.
Walk starts with pointer s; for each, advance the ends pointer e when the next end ≤ current start.
